>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"get"}
  path={"/oauth/token"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Browser-redirect flow: exchanges a provider authorization code for a WordPress
session and redirects the browser to the WordPress admin (or login page on failure).
The provider must be enabled in the plugin settings.

Supported providers: `google`, `auth0`, `facebook`, `github`.

Auth codes, IP allow-lists and the "Authentication enabled" setting do not apply to
this endpoint; only the provider must be enabled.

**Login start** - `provider` only (no `code`, no `error`): the login buttons point
here. The plugin stores a random `state` in a 10-minute HttpOnly cookie
(`sjl_oauth_state_<provider>`) and answers `302` to the provider's consent screen
with that `state`.

**Callback** - the provider redirects back with `code` and `state`. The callback is
only accepted when `state` matches the cookie of the same browser (login CSRF
protection); the cookie is single use. Otherwise the code is not exchanged and the
browser is redirected to the login page with an error (`error_code` 129 in the audit
log). Links that send visitors straight to the provider, without the login start,
are rejected.

If the OAuth identity matches an existing WordPress user (by email), the user is
logged in. If no match is found and "Register on OAuth login" is enabled, a new
user is created automatically. On failure the browser is redirected to the
WordPress login page.

> **Note**: this endpoint is designed for browser redirect callbacks (OAuth consent
> screen `redirect_uri`). To obtain a JWT programmatically, use `POST /oauth/token`
> instead.
